title: Sparse-Anchor Monocular Depth Calibration: Low-Cost Metric Depth on a Raspberry Pi Using a Single Time-of-Flight Sensor
content: Only relative, scale-ambiguous depth can be recovered from a single RGB frame using monocular depth estimation networks, which restricts their direct application in tasks requiring real-world metric distance, such as low-cost robot navigation and obstacle avoidance. Current methods for scale recovery usually rely on dense depth sensors, LiDAR, or stereo camera pairs, each of which adds expense, power consumption, and system complexity that is frequently out of proportion for small, inexpensive robotics platforms. This paper introduces sparse-anchor monocular depth calibration, a technique that uses a single low-cost time-of-flight (ToF) distance reading as an anchor to rescale the per-pixel relative output of a CPU-only monocular depth network into metric depth. The system aims for an end-to-end implementation on a Raspberry Pi 3B using a VL53L0X ToF sensor over I2C and a Pi camera. Hardware bring-up and a preliminary reliability and accuracy characterization of the ToF ranging subsystem have been finished against tape-measure ground truth at this stage of development; the camera and monocular-depth pipeline are integrated in design but await on-device validation, and the complete calibrated-depth evaluation is reported as ongoing work (Section VI). Rather than a new depth-estimation architecture, we clearly characterize this as a systems contribution: real-time, single-sensor, low-cost metric depth on commodity embedded hardware.
